definition: Artificial Intelligence for Environment & Sustainability (ARIES) is an international non-profit research project hosted by the Basque Centre for Climate Change (BC3) headquartered in Bilbao, Spain.
details: It was created to integrate scientific computational models for environmental sustainability assessment and policy-making, through ecoinformatics.

explainer.lead: ARIES is an international non-profit research project that connects scientific computational models to support environmental sustainability assessment and policy-making. Its aim is to help different kinds of environmental knowledge work together when decisions depend on more than one model.

tiers.eli5: Imagine trying to understand how a town's choices affect nature, with different experts each using their own puzzle pieces. ARIES is a research project about fitting those pieces together so people can assess environmental sustainability and make policies. It does this through ecoinformatics, which means using computing to work with environmental information.
tiers.practitioner: ARIES applies ecoinformatics to integrate scientific computational models for environmental sustainability assessment and policy-making. The practical focus is model integration: connecting separate models so their combined results can inform an assessment or decision.
tiers.paperLevel: ARIES is an international non-profit research project hosted by the Basque Centre for Climate Change (BC3) in Bilbao, Spain. Its objective is the integration of scientific computational models, through ecoinformatics, for environmental sustainability assessment and policy-making.

explainer.example: Consider a policy team assessing a proposed land-use plan. Rather than treating each relevant scientific computational model as a separate result, the team could use the ARIES approach to integrate the models through ecoinformatics and use the combined sustainability assessment when considering the plan.

explainer.intuition: Environmental questions often span several scientific models, so a single model may not capture everything needed for an assessment. ARIES is built around the idea of integrating those models to produce a more joined-up basis for sustainability decisions.
howItWorks: Start with an environmental sustainability or policy question.
Identify scientific computational models relevant to that question.
Use ecoinformatics to integrate the models.
Use the integrated assessment to inform policy-making.
explainer.whyItMatters: Sustainability policy can depend on evidence spread across separate scientific models. Integrating those models helps connect environmental assessment with the policy decisions it is meant to inform.
misconceptions: ARIES is a research project, not another name for its host, BC3.
Its focus is integrating scientific computational models, not supplying one standalone environmental model.
